title: Genesis Primitives are single-shot: once Invoked, no further Instances of them can ever exist
content:
Across all four Genesis Primitives in A.6.1.1.4.2.1, the In Progress Invocations Directory carries the same declaration rather than a list. For Agent Creation (A.6.1.1.4.2.1.1.1.4): "Because the Agent Creation Primitive is deployed solely for the one-time creation of the Agent, no further Instances of the Primitive can be Invoked." Prime Transformation and Executor Transformation repeat it verbatim for transformation; Agent Token (A.6.1.1.4.2.1.4.1.4) repeats it for "the one-time deployment of the Agent's token."

The Operational Process Definitions confirm the same shape from the other side: "no further operational process is needed post-deployment" (A.6.1.1.4.2.1.1.3.1.2, A.6.1.1.4.2.1.2.3.1.2).

This draws a hard line through the Primitive catalogue. Genesis Primitives are *constitutive* — they bring an entity into existence or change what kind of entity it is — and are exhausted by their first use. Operational Primitives (A.6.1.1.4.2.2 onward) are *recurring* and keep live In Progress directories that actually route work.

The practical consequence is that an Agent's identity cannot be quietly re-run. There is no legitimate path to a second Agent Creation or a second Prime Transformation for Skybase, so changing what Skybase fundamentally is would require editing the Artifact itself rather than invoking a process — which routes the change through Sky Governance instead of Agent operations.
description: Agent Creation, Prime Transformation, Executor Transformation and Agent Token each declare further Invocation impossible, so their empty In Progress directories are structural rather than incidental.
